# Annual Leave Policy

Document family: `family.hr.annual-leave`
Version: 1.0
Effective: 1 January 2023
Synthetic engineering benchmark material

Full-time employees receive 28 days of paid annual leave including public holidays. Requests for five or more consecutive working days must be submitted at least four weeks in advance.

Managers should respond within ten working days. No more than five unused days may be carried into the next leave year with written approval.

# Family Leave Reference Table

Document family: `family.hr.family-leave`
Version: 1.0
Effective: 1 April 2025
Synthetic engineering benchmark material

| Leave type | Initial notice route | Internal contact |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Maternity or adoption | Tell the manager and upload evidence to the HR portal | People Team |
| Paternity | Submit the family-leave form | People Team |
| Unpaid parental leave | Give at least 21 days' notice | Line manager |
| Emergency dependants leave | Notify the duty manager as soon as practicable | Line manager |

This table summarises internal notification routes and does not replace statutory eligibility rules.

# Overtime and Additional Hours Procedure

Document family: `family.payroll.overtime`
Version: 1.0
Effective: 1 March 2025
Synthetic engineering benchmark material

Overtime or additional hours must be authorised by the duty manager before they are worked, except where immediate action is necessary to protect safety. The employee records the actual start, finish and unpaid break in the rota system.

Authorisation confirms business need; it does not override working-time or safe-staffing controls. Estimated hours must be corrected to actual hours before payroll approval.

# Workplace Pension Reference

Document family: `family.payroll.pension`
Version: 1.0
Effective: 1 May 2025
Synthetic engineering benchmark material

| Question | Internal route |
| --- | --- |
| Change contribution percentage | Employee self-service portal |
| Opt-out notice | Scheme provider within the statutory opt-out window |
| Missing deduction | Payroll query form |
| Investment choice | Scheme provider; Alderbridge does not give financial advice |

Managers must not recommend whether an employee should opt out of pension saving.

# Flexible Working Procedure

Document family: `family.hr.flexible-working`
Version: 1.0
Effective: 15 April 2024
Synthetic engineering benchmark material

Employees may make a statutory flexible-working request from their first day of employment. The written request must describe the proposed change and preferred start date.

A manager must consult before refusing a request and complete the process, including any appeal, within two months unless an extension is agreed. Approval is not automatic where safe staffing cannot be maintained.

# Mileage Claim Form

Document family: `family.payroll.mileage`
Version: 1.0
Effective: 1 May 2025
Synthetic engineering benchmark material

| Field | Entry |
| --- | --- |
| Journey date and business purpose | |
| Start and destination postcodes | |
| Business miles | |
| Normal commute deducted | |
| Manager approval | |

Record the shortest reasonable business route. Home-to-work commuting mileage is not claimable merely because the employee was asked to attend their usual workplace.

# Lone Working Risk Control Policy

Document family: `family.health-safety.lone-working`
Version: 1.0
Effective: 1 May 2025
Synthetic engineering benchmark material

Managers assess travel, location, task, communication, known behaviour and emergency-access risks before lone work is allocated. Controls may include scheduled welfare calls, paired visits, personal alarms or a decision that the task cannot be completed alone.

If a welfare check is missed, the separate welfare-check procedure governs escalation. Staff must not treat a mobile phone signal as the only control where coverage is unreliable.

# Disciplinary Policy

Document family: `family.hr.disciplinary`
Version: 1.0
Effective: 1 March 2024
Synthetic engineering benchmark material

An investigatory meeting establishes facts and is not itself a disciplinary hearing. The employee must receive the allegation, evidence and possible consequences in writing before a formal hearing.

Suspension is a neutral precaution, not a disciplinary sanction, and must be reviewed every ten working days. Employees may be accompanied at a formal hearing by a trade union representative or workplace colleague.

# Safer Recruitment Policy

Document family: `family.hr.recruitment`
Version: 1.0
Effective: 1 March 2025
Synthetic engineering benchmark material

Care roles require identity and right-to-work checks, a complete employment history, two satisfactory references and the appropriate Disclosure and Barring Service check before unsupervised work.

A risk-assessed supervised start may be authorised only by the Director of People where the DBS update-service status is confirmed and all other checks are complete. A pending first-time DBS application does not permit unsupervised work.

# Employee Expenses Procedure

Document family: `family.payroll.expenses`
Version: 1.0
Effective: 1 April 2025
Synthetic engineering benchmark material

Expense claims require an itemised receipt and must be submitted within thirty calendar days of the purchase. The cost centre manager approves business purpose; Payroll checks tax and evidence requirements.

Alcohol, personal subscriptions and ordinary home-to-work travel are not reimbursable. A missing receipt declaration may be used only where replacement evidence cannot reasonably be obtained.

# Moving and Handling Policy

Document family: `family.health-safety.moving-handling`
Version: 1.0
Effective: 1 October 2023
Synthetic engineering benchmark material

Staff follow the person's moving-and-handling plan and use the named equipment. Two staff are required for every full-body hoist transfer. Any equipment defect is reported and the equipment removed from use.

The plan is reviewed annually or after a fall, material mobility change or equipment change.

# New Starter Induction Programme

Document family: `family.training.induction`
Version: 1.0
Effective: 1 January 2025
Synthetic engineering benchmark material

New starters complete corporate induction within their first ten working days. Before working without direct supervision they must complete local fire orientation, safeguarding awareness, infection-control essentials and role-specific moving-and-handling instruction.

The manager records induction completion in the learning system and resolves any missed topic before the employee's first unsupervised shift.

# New Starter Information Form

Document family: `family.hr.new-starter-form`
Version: 1.0
Effective: 19 May 2025
Synthetic engineering benchmark material

| Field | Required information |
| --- | --- |
| Preferred name | Name used at work |
| Emergency contact | Name, relationship and telephone number |
| Payroll | Bank details supplied through the secure HR portal |
| Adjustments | Workplace adjustment discussion requested: yes or no |

Do not email bank details or identity documents with this form. The manager records only whether secure documents have been received.

# Sickness Absence Procedure

Document family: `family.hr.sickness-absence`
Version: 1.0
Effective: 1 March 2023
Synthetic engineering benchmark material

Employees must telephone their line manager personally at least one hour before the shift begins. A text message is not sufficient unless an emergency prevents a call.

A return-to-work conversation is completed after every absence. A fit note is required from the eighth calendar day of continuous absence.

# Records Retention Schedule

Document family: `family.gdpr.retention`
Version: 1.0
Effective: 1 May 2025
Synthetic engineering benchmark material

| Record | Retention trigger | Retention period |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Unsuccessful applicant file | Recruitment decision | 6 months |
| Employee personnel file | Employment ends | 6 years |
| Adult social care record | Care ends | 8 years |
| Visitor sign-in record | Date of visit | 12 months |

A legal hold suspends routine deletion for the records named in the hold.

# Outbreak Visiting Restrictions Procedure

Document family: `family.visitors.outbreak-restrictions`
Version: 1.0
Effective: 1 October 2023
Synthetic engineering benchmark material

During a declared outbreak, routine indoor visiting is paused for all residents. Essential end-of-life visits require manager approval and visitors must follow the PPE instructions given on arrival.

The manager reviews restrictions every seven days with infection-control advice.

Changes received after the cut-off normally move to the following payroll.

Version: 1.0
Effective: 1 April 2024
Synthetic engineering benchmark material

| Field | Record |
|---|---|
| Person | Name and care-record identifier |
| Assistance | Mobility, communication and sensory support |
| Route | Primary and alternative evacuation routes |
| Equipment | Evacuation aid and trained operators |
| Staffing | Minimum assistance and role allocation |
| Review | Six-month review date or earlier trigger |

# Compliments and Feedback Procedure

Document family: `family.complaints.feedback`
Version: 1.0
Effective: 1 April 2025
Synthetic engineering benchmark material

Compliments and suggestions are logged separately from complaints but reviewed together for service-learning themes. Anonymous feedback is accepted and should record the channel, service and subject without attempting to identify the sender.

Feedback that alleges harm, abuse or a service failure is reclassified and routed through the appropriate safeguarding, incident or complaints process.

# Safeguarding Training Levels Reference

Document family: `family.training.safeguarding`
Version: 1.0
Effective: 1 April 2025
Synthetic engineering benchmark material

| Role | Required learning | Renewal |
| --- | --- | --- |
| All employees | Safeguarding adults awareness | Every 12 months |
| Care and support staff | Applied safeguarding adults | Every 12 months |
| Registered managers | Safeguarding decision-making and referrals | Every 24 months plus annual update |
| Board members | Governance oversight | Every 24 months |

Role changes trigger a review of the required level; the next annual refresher is not always sufficient.

# Midlands Lone Worker Welfare Check Procedure

Document family: `family.hr.lone-worker-welfare`
Version: 1.0
Effective: 1 May 2025
Synthetic engineering benchmark material

This procedure applies to the Midlands Region, including the Coventry community team. A lone community worker checks in through the rota system at the start and end of each visit.

If an end-of-visit check-in is fifteen minutes overdue, the coordinator calls the worker. If there is no response after a further ten minutes, the coordinator follows the emergency escalation contact and considers police assistance according to the known risk.

# Contractor Sign-In and Permit Form

Document family: `family.visitors.contractor-sign-in`
Version: 1.0
Effective: 1 April 2025
Synthetic engineering benchmark material

| Field | Entry |
| --- | --- |
| Company and engineer | |
| Arrival and departure time | |
| Work area and permit number | |
| Asbestos register checked where intrusive work is planned | Yes / No / Not applicable |
| Site contact | |

The site contact isolates the work area where required. A visitor badge does not replace a permit to work.

# Medication Competency Assessment

Document family: `family.training.medication-competency`
Version: 1.0
Effective: 1 January 2024
Synthetic engineering benchmark material

| Assessment element | Required evidence |
| --- | --- |
| MAR reading | Correctly identifies medicine, dose and time |
| Administration | Three directly observed medication rounds |
| PRN | Explains indication and records outcome |

Competency is reassessed every twelve months and after a significant medication error.

# Fire Safety Training Record

Document family: `family.training.fire`
Version: 1.0
Effective: 1 April 2025
Synthetic engineering benchmark material

| Field | Record |
| --- | --- |
| Employee and location | |
| Local alarm and call-point orientation | Date and assessor |
| Evacuation method and assembly point | Date and assessor |
| Practical drill participation | Date and role |
| Follow-up action | Owner and due date |

Watching the corporate fire video does not replace site-specific orientation or participation in practical drills.

# Complaints Handling Policy

Document family: `family.complaints.handling`
Version: 1.0
Effective: 1 July 2023
Synthetic engineering benchmark material

Staff acknowledge a complaint within three working days. The investigating manager aims to issue the written outcome within twenty working days and explains any unavoidable delay.

A complaint may be verbal or written. Staff must not require the complainant to complete a form before concerns are recorded.

# Mandatory Training Matrix

Document family: `family.training.matrix`
Version: 1.0
Effective: 1 January 2026
Synthetic engineering benchmark material

| Role or activity | Learning requirement | Refresher interval |
|---|---|---|
| All employees | Adult safeguarding awareness | 12 months |
| Care worker | Moving and handling | 12 months |
| Care worker | Infection prevention and control | 12 months |
| Staff who administer medicines | Medicines administration and observed competency | 12 months |
| Fire marshal | Fire marshal practical course | 24 months |
| Office-only employee | General fire safety awareness | 24 months |

Training must be completed before the recorded expiry date. A manager may require
an earlier reassessment following an incident, prolonged absence or material
change in duties.

# Data Protection Policy

Document family: `family.gdpr.data-protection`
Version: 1.0
Effective: 1 January 2024
Synthetic engineering benchmark material

Personal information must be collected for a defined purpose, limited to what is necessary, kept accurate and retained only as long as required. Staff must lock paper records away and use approved systems for electronic records.

Suspected disclosure to the wrong person must be reported to the Data Protection Officer within twenty-four hours.

# Resident Isolation Risk Assessment

Document family: `family.infection.isolation`
Version: 1.0
Effective: 1 October 2025
Synthetic engineering benchmark material

| Assessment area | Record |
|---|---|
| Infection risk | Organism, symptoms, transmission route and clinical advice |
| Capacity and consent | Decision-specific assessment and person's wishes |
| Harms of restriction | Distress, mobility, nutrition, social contact and liberty |
| Alternatives | Cohorting, ventilation, PPE and adjusted activities |
| Support plan | Communication, meaningful activity and review frequency |
| End point | Clear criteria for reducing or ending restrictions |

Isolation is never imposed solely because it is convenient for staffing.

# Grievance Procedure

Document family: `family.hr.grievance`
Version: 1.0
Effective: 1 March 2024
Synthetic engineering benchmark material

Employees should normally raise a grievance in writing with their line manager. If the grievance concerns that manager, it must be sent to the next manager or People Team.

A grievance meeting should normally take place within seven working days. An appeal must be submitted within five working days of the written outcome.

# Safety Equipment Inspection Schedule

Document family: `family.health-safety.equipment-checks`
Version: 1.0
Effective: 1 April 2025
Synthetic engineering benchmark material

| Equipment | User check | Formal inspection |
|---|---|---|
| Mobile hoist | Before each use | Every 6 months |
| Passenger lift | Visual check daily | Thorough examination every 6 months |
| Evacuation chair | Monthly | Annual service |
| Portable electrical equipment | Before use | Risk-based test interval |
| Fire extinguisher | Monthly visual check | Annual service |

An inspection interval never authorises continued use of visibly damaged equipment.

# Care and Compliance Abbreviations

Document family: `family.reference.abbreviations`
Version: 1.0
Effective: 1 January 2026
Synthetic engineering benchmark material

| Abbreviation | Meaning |
|---|---|
| MAR | Medication Administration Record |
| PRN | Medicine prescribed to be given when required |
| MCA | Mental Capacity Act |
| DoLS | Deprivation of Liberty Safeguards |
| PPE | Personal protective equipment |
| COSHH | Control of Substances Hazardous to Health |
| RIDDOR | Reporting of Injuries, Diseases and Dangerous Occurrences Regulations |
| DBS | Disclosure and Barring Service |
| SAR | Subject access request |
| IPC | Infection prevention and control |

This reference expands organisational terminology. It does not replace the
substantive policy or procedure that governs an activity.

# Workplace Risk Assessment Form

Document family: `family.health-safety.risk-assessment`
Version: 1.0
Effective: 1 March 2025
Synthetic engineering benchmark material

| Required field | Record |
|---|---|
| Hazard | What could cause harm |
| People affected | Employees, people supported, visitors or contractors |
| Existing controls | Measures already operating |
| Risk rating | Likelihood and consequence before further action |
| Further action | Owner and completion date |
| Residual risk | Rating after controls |
| Review | Planned date and earlier triggers |

Generic phrases such as “staff to take care” are not adequate controls.

# Visitors and Contractors Procedure

Document family: `family.visitors.general`
Version: 1.0
Effective: 1 March 2025
Synthetic engineering benchmark material

## Arrival and identity

All visitors must sign in at reception and wear the issued visitor badge.
A contractor must additionally show photographic identification and be met by the
employee responsible for the work.

## Fire information

Reception staff tell visitors how to recognise the fire alarm and direct them to
the assembly arrangement for that location.
Visitors must not use lifts during an evacuation and must remain with their host or follow staff instructions.

## Confidentiality and infection precautions

Visitors must not photograph records, staff or people supported without explicit
authorisation. They must follow any displayed infection-control precautions and
postpone non-essential visits when they have symptoms of a transmissible illness.

## Departure

Visitors sign out, return their badge and notify reception if their host is no
longer available. The sign-in record is used during emergency roll calls.

# COSHH Assessment Procedure

Document family: `family.health-safety.coshh`
Version: 1.0
Effective: 1 March 2025
Synthetic engineering benchmark material

Before a hazardous substance is introduced, the manager obtains the current safety data sheet and completes a COSHH assessment covering exposure routes, storage, handling, PPE, spill response and disposal. Manufacturer instructions are evidence, not a substitute for the workplace assessment.

Assessments are reviewed annually and immediately after a formulation, task or control changes. Decanted products must retain an identifiable label; drink containers must never be used.

# Injury Body Map Form

Document family: `family.safeguarding.body-map`
Version: 1.0
Effective: 1 May 2025
Synthetic engineering benchmark material

| Required field | Guidance |
|---|---|
| Person and date | Stable care-record identifier and observation time |
| Location | Mark the diagram and describe the anatomical location |
| Appearance | Size, colour, shape and observable condition |
| Account | Record the person's own words without interpretation |
| Action | First aid, clinical advice, safeguarding and notifications |

Do not guess the cause of an injury. Use body maps to record observable facts; they do not replace an incident or safeguarding record.

# Controlled Drugs Procedure

Document family: `family.medication.controlled-drugs`
Version: 1.0
Effective: 1 June 2023
Synthetic engineering benchmark material

Two authorised members of staff must witness every controlled-drug administration and sign the controlled-drugs register immediately. The running balance is checked after each entry. A discrepancy is reported to the registered manager before the end of the shift and the stock is secured while the check is repeated.

Expired stock remains in the controlled-drugs cabinet, clearly segregated, until collected by the supplying pharmacy. Staff must not destroy controlled drugs without an authorised witness and the required record.

# Accident and Incident Reporting Procedure

Document family: `family.health-safety.accident-reporting`
Version: 1.0
Effective: 1 July 2023
Synthetic engineering benchmark material

Staff first make the area safe, provide first aid and obtain emergency assistance. Every accident, near miss or dangerous occurrence is recorded before the end of the shift. The manager reviews whether the event may be reportable under RIDDOR and contacts the health and safety lead within two working days.

# PRN Medicines Protocol

Document family: `family.medication.prn`
Version: 1.0
Effective: 1 March 2025
Synthetic engineering benchmark material

PRN means medicine prescribed to be given when required. Before offering a PRN medicine, staff must check the person's current protocol for the indication, minimum interval, maximum dose in 24 hours and non-medicine measures to try first. A PRN entry on the MAR is not, by itself, enough information to administer safely.

Staff record the reason for the dose, time, quantity and observed outcome. If the medicine is ineffective, requested unusually often or refused when symptoms remain concerning, the shift leader must review the care plan and obtain clinical advice. PRN medicine must never be used for staff convenience or as an unrecorded response to distress.

# Midlands Emergency Evacuation Procedure

Document family: `family.fire.midlands-evacuation`
Version: 1.0
Effective: 1 March 2025
Synthetic engineering benchmark material

This procedure applies to Oakfield Lodge and Willow Bank Community Service. Activate the alarm, call 999 and follow the local evacuation strategy. Oakfield staff use progressive horizontal evacuation; community staff leave by the nearest safe exit.

The regional fallback assembly point is the signed delivery-area muster point. The on-call manager is informed after emergency services have been contacted, never instead of calling 999.

# Fire Drill and Debrief Procedure

Document family: `family.fire.drills`
Version: 1.0
Effective: 1 April 2023
Synthetic engineering benchmark material

Each service completes a fire drill at least every six months. Drills should rotate across shifts so night staff participate at least annually. The record includes alarm time, evacuation duration, staff present, simulated conditions and actions agreed.

The registered manager reviews the drill within five working days and assigns actions with owners and dates.

Version: 1.0
Effective: 1 January 2023
Synthetic engineering benchmark material

Full-time employees receive 28 days of paid annual leave including public holidays. Requests for five or more consecutive working days must be submitted at least four weeks in advance.

Managers should respond within ten working days. No more than five unused days may be carried into the next leave year with written approval.
